88aa8c9e12f1b617.lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday, when both the Telluride Housing Authority and Town Council take up the same consequential question: whether to strip the maximum sale price from two town-constructed units at 215 East Colorado Avenue — FINO 1A and 2A — converting them from affordable ownership units to employee dwelling units, a structural change to how those homes work in the local housing stock. Council also holds public hearings on the sale of Spruce House Unit H. On the 24th, Telluride's P&Z holds a work session on an early-stage employee housing proposal at the school district site on West Colorado, and San Miguel County hosts a regional five-county discussion about a gas pipeline spill involving the Southern Ute Indian Council.

Thursday brings a full slate: a **Special Meeting - Planning & Zoning Commission**, a **Town Council Budget** session, the **Lodging Tax Panel Meeting**, and the **Design Review Board**, where two multifamily projects are on the table — 15 employee apartments at 306 Adams Ranch Rd and four new units at 100 Pennington Pl. On the lighter side, Monday's **Bike & Brewery Tour** rolls from Mountain Village down to Telluride Brewing Co., **Ken Gentry & the Companions** play The Alibi on Thursday, and Saturday Ouray throws a free 150th anniversary concert at Fellin Park headlined by **Big Head Todd & the Monsters**.
